title: GW150914 · gravitational waves (Draft)
description: The same plan as Drafts only: a start Card and three Drafts that state what each step takes and gives, ready for the Agent's "Generate Cards".

cards.summary: Fetches the H1 and L1 strain data of GW150914 published by GWOSC (4 kHz, 32 s of HDF5) and passes them to the next Card as a folder. Shows the size and SHA-256 of the files fetched.

cards.summary: Whitens H1 and L1 with a PSD from Welch's method over 4-second segments, and applies a band-pass from f_low to f_high Hz (the pass band is a parameter). Shows the waveform around the event as a line chart, and passes the whitened series on.

cards.summary: Shifts L1 within ±10 ms (its sign may flip too) to find the delay at which it best overlaps H1, overlays them, and shows an image with H1's spectrogram revealing the chirp (the frequency rising). Also finds a rough SNR against the noise, kept in the image and a table.

notes.html:
GW150914

On 14 September 2015, the two LIGO detectors (Hanford H1, Livingston L1) observed, for the first time, two black holes merging.

Whitening divides by the noise spectrum Sn(f)S_n(f) to even out the weight of each frequency.

h~w(f)=h~(f)Sn(f)\tilde h_w(f) = \frac{\tilde h(f)}{\sqrt{S_n(f)}}

Just before the merger, the gravitational wave's frequency rises as f∝(tc−t)−3/8f \propto (t_c - t)^{-3/8} (the chirp).

Change the pass band of whiten (f_low, f_high) and rerun just that Card.

intro: A Draft is a Card that says in words what it receives, what it does and what it passes on. It has no code yet. With "Generate Cards" in the app, the Agent writes code from these words, runs it and checks.
